lines.sub: So how many fake addresses does it take to climb this ladder, from the median up to the top?
lines.tts: So how many fake addresses does it take to climb this ladder, from the median up to the top?

lines.sub: Each point of the tower on the left is one contract of the matched cohort.
lines.tts: Each point of the tower on the left is one contract of the matched cohort.

lines.sub: The height is the EndorseRank score on a log scale, so each level up means a score ten times larger.
lines.tts: The height is the EndorseRank score on a log scale, so each level up means a score ten times larger.

lines.sub: Most contracts sit close to the floor.
lines.tts: Most contracts sit close to the floor.

lines.sub: The box in the middle is the target contract, whose score the attacker wants to raise.
lines.tts: The box in the middle is the target contract, whose score the attacker wants to raise.

lines.sub: It starts at c, the score of an address that nobody approves. That is 7.64 × 10⁻⁸.
lines.tts: It starts at c, the score of an address that nobody approves. That is seven point six four times ten to the minus eight.

lines.sub: The counter on the right will show how many fake addresses are needed.
lines.tts: The counter on the right will show how many fake addresses are needed.

lines.sub: First rung: the median. It is very cheap.
lines.tts: First rung, the median. It is very cheap.

lines.sub: It is enough for two addresses, the target contract and one fake address, to approve each other.
lines.tts: It is enough for two addresses, the target contract and one fake address, to approve each other.

lines.sub: The pink dashed circle is that partner, and the pair needs two approvals, one each way.
lines.tts: The pink dashed circle is that partner, and the pair needs two approvals, one each way.

lines.sub: In the star formula from the last slide, f counts the fake addresses and d is the damping factor.
lines.tts: In the star formula from the last slide, f counts the fake addresses and d is the damping factor.

lines.sub: Putting f = 1 into that formula gives c(1 + d) / (1 − d²).
lines.tts: Putting f equals one into that formula gives c times the quantity one plus d, divided by the quantity one minus the square of d.

lines.sub: Since 1 − d² = (1 − d)(1 + d), the factor (1 + d) cancels, leaving c / (1 − d).
lines.tts: Since one minus the square of d is the product of one minus d and one plus d, the factor one plus d cancels, leaving c divided by the quantity one minus d.

lines.sub: That is 5.09 × 10⁻⁷, which is above the median.
lines.tts: That is five point zero nine times ten to the minus seven, which is above the median.

lines.sub: Solving the formula for f gives f ≤ 0, so the thesis says that no farm is needed.
lines.tts: Solving the formula for f gives f less than or equal to zero, so the thesis says that no farm is needed.

lines.sub: But approving each other takes a partner, so in practice the attacker creates 1 fake address.
lines.tts: But approving each other takes a partner, so in practice the attacker creates one fake address.

lines.sub: Next rung: the 90th percentile is passed with 22 fake addresses.
lines.tts: Next rung. The ninetieth percentile is passed with twenty-two fake addresses.

lines.sub: That is 44 approvals per window.
lines.tts: That is forty-four approvals per window.

lines.sub: In the tower, the target box has climbed to the 90th-percentile ring.
lines.tts: In the tower, the target box has climbed to the ninetieth-percentile ring.

lines.sub: The 99th percentile takes 2,074 fake addresses.
lines.tts: The ninety-ninth percentile takes two thousand and seventy-four fake addresses.

lines.sub: At two approvals per address, that makes 4,148 per window.
lines.tts: At two approvals per address, that makes four thousand one hundred and forty-eight per window.

lines.sub: The pink points now gather around the target box.
lines.tts: The pink points now gather around the target box.

lines.sub: The numbers start to grow fast.
lines.tts: The numbers start to grow fast.

lines.sub: Reaching the top takes more than 130,000 fake addresses.
lines.tts: Reaching the top takes more than one hundred thirty thousand fake addresses.

lines.sub: The counter reads about 135,895.
lines.tts: The counter reads about one hundred thirty-five thousand eight hundred ninety-five.

lines.sub: That is more than 270,000 approvals per window.
lines.tts: That is more than two hundred seventy thousand approvals per window.

lines.sub: Each point of the pink haze covering the tower stands for five fake addresses.
lines.tts: Each point of the pink haze covering the tower stands for five fake addresses.

lines.sub: Note that this calculation leaves out one effect.
lines.tts: Note that this calculation leaves out one effect.

lines.sub: A farm this large would also raise the total number of nodes, and so lower c.
lines.tts: A farm this large would also raise the total number of nodes, and so lower c.

lines.sub: Why is the top this expensive? Because endorsement is concentrated.
lines.tts: Why is the top this expensive? Because endorsement is concentrated.

lines.sub: The top contract holds about 3% of the whole graph's share, more than 400,000 times c.
lines.tts: The top contract holds about three percent of the whole graph's share, more than four hundred thousand times c.

lines.sub: In short, looking ordinary is cheap, and the top is expensive.
lines.tts: In short, looking ordinary is cheap, and the top is expensive.

lines.sub: That is why this study concludes that none of its scores should be used on its own to raise a warning or to set a reward.
lines.tts: That is why this study concludes that none of its scores should be used on its own to raise a warning or to set a reward.

lines.sub: Cutting the tokens down to five does not change the attack cost.
lines.tts: Cutting the tokens down to five does not change the attack cost.

lines.sub: That is because approving one of those tokens costs the attacker no more than approving any other token.
lines.tts: That is because approving one of those tokens costs the attacker no more than approving any other token.

lines.sub: In the interactive version of these slides, a slider on the right sets f, and the box height and the number of pink points follow the formula.
lines.tts: In the interactive version of these slides, a slider on the right sets f, and the box height and the number of pink points follow the formula.

lines.sub: So much for attack cost. We also measured how fast the scores compute, as part of the revised analysis.
lines.tts: So much for attack cost. We also measured how fast the scores compute, as part of the revised analysis.

lines.sub: As I said in chapter 4, one PageRank iteration does one multiplication per edge.
lines.tts: As I said in chapter four, one PageRank iteration does one multiplication per edge.

lines.sub: Look at the small world at the top right. It has four edges.
lines.tts: Look at the small world at the top right. It has four edges.

lines.sub: So one iteration is multiplications 1 to 4, four in all.
lines.tts: So one iteration is multiplications one to four, four in all.

lines.sub: The circled numbers are the order of the multiplications, not edge weights.
lines.tts: The circled numbers are the order of the multiplications, not edge weights.

lines.sub: The derivation box below says the same in symbols.
lines.tts: The derivation box below says the same in symbols.

lines.sub: So first, the edge counts of the two graphs.
lines.tts: So first, the edge counts of the two graphs.

lines.sub: On the same contracts, the allowance graph, which EndorseRank walks, has 11,210,114 edges.
lines.tts: On the same contracts, the allowance graph, which EndorseRank walks, has eleven million two hundred ten thousand one hundred fourteen edges.

lines.sub: The transfer graph, which AWP walks, has 25,001,216, which is 2.23 times as many.
lines.tts: The transfer graph, which A W P walks, has twenty-five million one thousand two hundred sixteen, which is two point two three times as many.

lines.sub: Each small arrow stands for 50,000 edges.
lines.tts: Each small arrow stands for fifty thousand edges.

lines.sub: Building the matrix also takes one step per edge, so the amount of work is proportional to the number of edges.
lines.tts: Building the matrix also takes one step per edge, so the amount of work is proportional to the number of edges.

lines.sub: Proportional means that twice the edges is twice the work.
lines.tts: Proportional means that twice the edges is twice the work.

lines.sub: As we saw at the start of this chapter, the solver graphs have slightly fewer nodes than in chapter 3.
lines.tts: As we saw at the start of this chapter, the solver graphs have slightly fewer nodes than in chapter three.

lines.sub: The solver leaves out addresses whose amounts are all so small that their value weight is zero.
lines.tts: The solver leaves out addresses whose amounts are all so small that their value weight is zero.

lines.sub: That is 2,602 on the allowance side and 2,246 on the transfer side.
lines.tts: That is two thousand six hundred and two on the allowance side, and two thousand two hundred and forty-six on the transfer side.

lines.sub: Now we start both computations at the same time, with the same solver.
lines.tts: Now we start both computations at the same time, with the same solver.

lines.sub: The screen runs 4 times faster than real time, and the clock shows real seconds.
lines.tts: The screen runs four times faster than real time, and the clock shows real seconds.

lines.sub: Each time is the mean of five timed runs after one warm-up run.
lines.tts: Each time is the mean of five timed runs after one warm-up run.

lines.sub: EndorseRank finished in 10.29 seconds.
lines.tts: EndorseRank finished in ten point two nine seconds.

lines.sub: AWP finished in 22.37 seconds.
lines.tts: A W P finished in twenty-two point three seven seconds.

lines.sub: AWP took 2.17 times as long, and it has 2.23 times as many edges.
lines.tts: A W P took two point one seven times as long, and it has two point two three times as many edges.

lines.sub: The iteration counts differ a little, 69 and 92.
lines.tts: The iteration counts differ a little, sixty-nine and ninety-two.

lines.sub: But the time ratio stays very close to the edge ratio.
lines.tts: But the time ratio stays very close to the edge ratio.

lines.sub: So EndorseRank is faster not because its algorithm is better, but because the allowance graph is sparse.
lines.tts: So EndorseRank is faster not because its algorithm is better, but because the allowance graph is sparse.
